children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI linked stocks continued to pull back as Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Zooming in on Everpure

Everpure’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 50 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Everpure and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock gained 5.1% on the news that the company reported fiscal third-quarter results that topped analyst consensus estimates and raised its full-year revenue and operating income guidance.

According to the company's earnings release, Everpure generated product revenue of $948 million, up 77% year on year, and subscription services revenue of $512 million, up 19%, in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 ended November 1, 2026. The company reported total revenue of $1.46 billion, up 51.4% year on year, which topped aggregate analyst estimates sourced from S&P Capital IQ of $1.33 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of 86 cents exceeded the consensus estimate of 78 cents. Revenue guidance for the following quarter of $1.51 billion at the midpoint also beat analyst consensus estimates of $1.49 billion. The release also showed non-GAAP operating income of $345 million, a 23.6% non-GAAP operating margin and free cash flow of $265 million, and CFO Tarek Robbiati said in the release that the company raised its full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter.

CEO Charlie Giancarlo said on the earnings call that the vast majority of dollar revenue growth came from the core business, while percentage growth in newer areas including hyperscale solutions, scale AI and modern data software outpaced the company average.

Everpure is up 32.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $91.71 per share, it is still trading 41.6% below its 52-week high of $156.97 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Everpure’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $3,337.
